args.prompt:
Create a NEW Scandinavian bedroom photograph from scratch, portrait 4:5; do not reference or recreate any previous generated room. Reference 1 is the exact current framed product and the authority for its geometry; reference 2 is the complete original snowy-pine art; reference 3 is a board of individual real product/material examples, not a room to copy. Generate the art naturally inside the room photograph, under the same light and glass reflections, never paste it afterward.

Composition: step back to show a full 205 cm pine single bed in SIDE VIEW across the room, including both end posts and the entire long wooden side rail. Its long side runs nearly horizontally from about x=285 to x=1090 on a 1122-pixel-wide portrait canvas, parallel and square to the pale-blue wall. The pillow is at the LEFT end. Set the real burgundy flecked Normann Bit stool by that pillow, fully inside the picture around x=115–260, carrying the real white-bowl stone-base Kizu lamp, also fully visible. Let a left window and beige curtain enter only at the left edge. A green narrow-striped cotton duvet naturally covers the bed, with matching pillow and an open book near the pillow. A pale-grey textured wool rug lies partly under the bed, with slippers in the walkway. Pine floorboards and white skirting; no extra artworks or unrelated furniture.

Hang the small framed Pines print over the LEFT pillow, around x=350–550, leaving calm wall around it. Its actual portrait paper is 45 cm wide and 60 cm tall, outer frame 47.4 × 62.4 cm with 12 mm oak rails. Near frontal view: visible OUTER frame width approximately 205–215 pixels and height approximately 270–282 pixels, ratio exactly 0.760; white paper ratio exactly 0.750; inner photograph 42 × 56 cm, ratio exactly 0.750. Do NOT draw a tall skinny rectangle. The frame width is 23% of the BED's 205 cm visible length, 1.32 times the fully visible 36 cm stool width, and 1.90 times the fully visible 25 cm lamp-bowl width, allowing for slight foreground perspective. White border 1.5 cm each side and 2 cm top/bottom, narrow and proportional. Preserve the entire source art: many stars, blue-black sky, high snow-covered pines to left and right, shorter central pine, snow foreground; no moon, crop, stretch or shifted tree silhouettes.

Editorial real-interior atmosphere. Level standing camera about 150 cm, moderate lens, physically coherent side window daylight from the left with darker sheltered undersides and gentle shadow away from window. Fine distinct cotton stripe weave, wool rug loops, pine grain and glossy-flecked solid stool; coherent subdued glazing/reflection in the frame. No over-sharpened textile ripples, plastic smoothing, CGI or uniformly bright HDR. Slightly lived-in, believable photographic scale and material quality. No text, labels or logos.

prompts.sheep_test03: Create one entirely NEW, photorealistic premium Scandinavian art-shop room photograph. This is a fresh room generation, not an edit of any prior rendered room. Three references: image 1 is the exact finished framed product and governs the print geometry, narrow white border, thin natural-oak frame and original artwork; image 2 is the full-resolution artwork and governs every photographic detail inside the frame; image 3 is a product/material board and governs only the named furniture and materials, not its pictured rooms. Place the image-1 print as a real glass-fronted wall object in a calm child's drawing/study corner. The real paper is precisely 40 cm wide by 50 cm high, portrait 4:5. The natural oak moulding is 12 mm each side, so the visible outside frame is about 42.4 by 52.4 cm, width:height 0.809. Paper and artwork must NOT become a skinny portrait. Keep the art's uncropped 4:5 photograph with proportional narrow white margin (about 1.5 cm each side and 1.875 cm at top and bottom, leaving 37 by 46.25 cm artwork). The photo is the original scene under a dense, near-black leafy tree arch opening onto a clearing, with a damp two-rut track and puddles leading forward. Preserve the EXACT sheep group from reference 2: eight sheep as visible, including the small pale sheep in the distant left clearing, the light sheep near the left foreground, the large dark one near the centre foreground, the dark one standing at right, and the clustered dark animals behind. Maintain their relative positions and scale. Do not simplify to a generic flock, invent sheep, alter the track, remove foliage, crop, stretch or recolour the art. Room: left-side wall of soft off-white Chi limewash, honest honey oak plank floor, large ivory looped-wool rug with individually visible yarn loops. Under and beside the framed print, the exact Ferm Living Little Architect yellow table and ash child's chair from board. One restrained set of pencils and paper on the table; natural rattan apple basket on the floor. Natural window daylight from off camera right, contact shadows, subtle wall and glazing reflections. Straight architectural walls, table/chair legs structurally sound and square, rug texture not melted. Quiet high-end editorial interior photograph, 35 mm lens at child-height-to-mid-height with enough wall and floor visible to judge physical scale. No people, no other wall art, no text, no floating objects, no decorative sheep toy. Crucially: the framed object's outer rectangle must remain 42.4:52.4 and the inner photographed image 4:5 in the finished room view.

prompts.sheep_test04:
Create a NEW photorealistic close editorial interior photograph of a child's drawing desk, as a fresh image generation. Never use any earlier rendered room. Reference image 1 is the exact framed wall product; reference 2 is the original source artwork; reference 3 supplies the exact named furniture/material pieces only. The hero is the actual framed print from image 1, large in the photograph, occupying approximately 500 pixels width and 620 pixels height on a 1122×1402 output. The framed print is physical 40×50 cm paper, portrait 4:5, with 12 mm natural oak rails, so its OUTER dimensions are exactly 42.4 cm wide by 52.4 cm high, outer ratio 0.809. Its inner original photograph stays 4:5 without crop, stretch or recomposition; use a narrow proportional white border about 1.5 cm horizontally and 1.875 cm vertically. Put this framed print flat on the wall above the exact mustard-yellow Ferm Living Little Architect child's table, with a small part of the ash child's chair visible from the right and the natural woven rattan apple basket partly visible at bottom left. Camera is substantially closer than a full-room shot, nearly straight-on, so the print has enough resolved pixels for artwork fidelity. Desk may crop at sides or bottom naturally, but framed print is fully shown. Keep room sparse, tactile and honest: off-white softly textured wall, honey oak plank floor glimpse, natural daylight from window off camera right, pencil pot and one sheet of drawing paper. Do not add other wall art, toy sheep, people or text. 
Art fidelity is the top priority. The photograph INSIDE the frame must match reference 2 as closely as possible. It has a nearly black leafy canopy arch over a pale clearing, a green damp TWO-RUT track with visible puddle reflections, dark foliage at both sides and bottom, and EXACTLY EIGHT separate sheep in the original relative locations: a small distant pale sheep at rear far left; the light sheep on the left foreground track; a large dark sheep in the centre-right foreground; a dark sheep standing at right side; and four more dark/mottled sheep in the middle cluster between those. Preserve the eight bodies individually, their spacing and orientation as seen in reference 2. Do not turn them into blotches, remove one, change species, or invent extra sheep. Do not brighten or stylise the dark woodland. Keep thin oak frame corners square, white border straight and evenly proportioned, wall shadow and glass reflection subtle. Real wood grain, crisp furniture joinery, no melted surfaces.
